title: feat(app-shell): an app's reports have an index, and the command palette finds them (objectui#13020)
body:
Fixes #13020
Clause-②: no

## What changes

An app's reports now have an index, and the command palette finds them. Before this, a report the app's navigation does not name had no UI path (HotCRM: 7 of its 10 reports), and the palette matched only the reports the navigation names.

- **Route `/apps/APP/reports`** (`AppReportIndexView`, new). It lists the reports the app's package ships, by localized label (`reportLabel` over the served label, as `useRecentItemLabel` names a report), sorted, each linking to `report/NAME`. It shows an empty state when there are none. The view is a `routeChunk.lazy` declaration with its `APP_ROUTE_CHUNKS` row (it preloads like every app route) and an `APP_ROUTE_METADATA_READS` row of `['report']`: it never reads the object registry.
- **Which reports an app ships** (`appReportIndex.ts`, new, internal): those whose `_packageId` is the app's, the owner link `preferLocal` and `AppHeader` resolve a report by. An app with no `_packageId` (created in the console) lists the reports no package owns.
- **Read rule.** A report is left out when any object its datasets read (`dataset`, or each `blocks[].dataset` of a joined report, through the dataset's `object`) fails `mayReadObject`, the console's one object-read verdict (`navObjectReadGate`, objectui#12109). Its inputs are the dataset list (one cached `/meta/dataset` read) and the permissions the shell already holds. An unknown answer refuses nothing, the posture of that gate.
- **Command palette.** While it is open inside an app, it reads the same entries and offers each report that no navigation entry names, under the Reports heading. A nav-entry report is still offered through its entry, once. A closed palette reads neither list.
- **Placement: one static sidebar entry, "All reports",** after the app's navigation and before Recent, in every app but Studio. I measured what the console already does. The sidebar's app arm holds the built-in, non-authored entries that open the app's content (Recent, Favorites). The header's one built-in content list is the Help menu's "this app's docs", which is help, not a place to work. The sidebar has no footer any more (objectui#12429), so the entry goes in the content. It is static: the sidebar is chrome on every route and reads no report list for it (objectui#12980). An app with no reports gets the index's empty state.
- New strings in all ten shipped locales: `sidebar.allReports` and `console.reportIndex.title / emptyTitle / emptyDescription`. They live in `packages/i18n/src/locales`, where the app-shell's console strings live. No new export. The changeset is `@object-ui/app-shell: minor` (a new user-visible route) plus `@object-ui/i18n: minor` (the new keys), and both packages are in the `fixed` group.

## Mechanism finding (the dispatch assumed otherwise)

The report page has **no** client-side read check. `ReportView` opens whatever report it is given, and a member who may not read the dataset's object gets the dataset query refused by the server. So the index cannot reuse "the report page's verdict". It uses the console's single object-read verdict (`mayReadObject`) on the report's dataset objects, which is the check that predicts that refusal. No new verdict was written.

## Tests (all on head `ffa69001f8`)

- New `views/__tests__/AppReportIndex-13020.test.tsx`, 8 tests, run through the real `MetadataProvider`, `MePermissionsProvider`, `ExpressionProvider` and `I18nProvider`:
  - (a) a report the navigation does not name appears in the index (with its link) and in the palette;
  - (b) a report on an unreadable object appears in neither, nor does a joined report with one such block;
  - CONTROLS: the nav-entry report is offered once in the palette, and another package's report appears in neither surface. The index reads `report` and `dataset` and never `object`. A closed palette reads neither list. An app that ships no report shows the empty state.
- New `layout/__tests__/UnifiedSidebar.reportIndexLink-13020.test.tsx`, 3 tests: the entry links `/apps/crm/reports` for an app whose navigation names no report, drawing it reads no report list, and (CONTROL) the app's own entries are unchanged.
- `appRouteChunks-12980.test.ts` now also asserts that both the route table and `APP_ROUTE_CHUNKS` map `reports` to `AppReportIndexView`. The table-wide pins in that file and in `appRouteMetadataReads-12809` stay green, so the new route has both rows.
- Two existing sidebar pins enumerate rows, and both are updated in their own commit. In `favoritesMenu-12427`, `menuRows` now skips the report index row: it is not a navigation entry and has no row menu. In `iconModeLabelFocus-12795`, the tab walk now ends on "All reports".
- **Ablation, run once.** The read filter's predicate, `mayOpenReport(report, datasetObjects, can)`, was replaced by an always-true one through `ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor went from 1 to 0 and the blob from `80798304671f` to `979ce2058a9e`. Result: 3 tests failed and 5 passed. The failures were index (b), the palette (a)/(b) case, and the index control that lists the exact entries. After the restore, the blob equals HEAD (`80798304671f`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Family runs under the shared lock, `vitest run --maxWorkers=1`, over every app-shell and i18n test file whose name matches CommandPalette / AppContent / appRouteChunks / report / AppHeader / UnifiedSidebar / locale / i18n (232 files):
  - app-shell batches: 60 files / 451 tests, 60 / 379, and 28 / 496, all passed (the second was re-run after the two pin updates);
  - i18n: 84 files, 1319 passed and 13 skipped.
- Type-check: closure build `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...` (28 tasks), then `type-check` for `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/app-shell`. Both exited 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the three new or edited test files.
- Gates, each exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `control-bytes` and `new-line-citations`, plus `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` and `check-changeset-presence.mjs`.
- Lint, narrowed to the changed files: the root `eslint.config.js` (not type-aware: no `projectService` and no type-checked preset) over the 19 changed TS/TSX files with `--no-inline-config --format json`. The JSON counts 19 files, 0 errors and 63 warnings. No warning sits on an added line, and the new files have none. Because the config is not type-aware, the change cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. The two later test edits were linted the same way and exited 0.
- Declared to CI: the full `packages/app-shell/` directory run.
- NOT MEASURED: a real browser run of the console (reason: unit and DOM pins only, under container contention).

## Acceptance notes

- `reports` is a static segment, so it outranks `:objectName`. An object literally named `reports` would have its list page shadowed by the index, as one named `search` already is. Not filed: no such object is known.
- A navigation entry of type `report` is still drawn without a read check in the sidebar and the palette, as before (objectui#12109 left report entries to their target). The new verdict could gate those entries too. That would change the nav-entry path, which this card pins as unchanged. Carrier: none.
- The filter reads the spec's `dataset` / `blocks[].dataset` only. A pre-spec report stored with `objectName` or `dataSource.object` keys is not read-gated here (contract-first, AGENTS.md #0.1). The server still refuses its query.
